title: Interactive 3D HTML Embedding & Video Texture Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/RTHTML_AND_RTVIEW_RICH_MEDIA_ARCHITECTURE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/RTHTML_AND_RTVIEW_RICH_MEDIA_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/RTHTML_AND_RTVIEW_RICH_MEDIA_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Bridging standard Web DOM elements (interactive UI, iframes, live documentation, forms) and streaming video into a hardware-accelerated 3D WebGPU world requires hybrid rendering strategies.

items: **[`RTHTML`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/RTHTML.ts)**: A 3D model entity projecting live HTML/DOM content onto an oriented 3D plane, featuring 4 rendering modes, invisible boundary clipping, and bidirectional pointer raycast forwarding.

**[`RTVideo`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/RTVideo.ts) & [`VideoData`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/VideoData.ts)**: 3D video playback surface binding HTML5 `<video>` streams to GPU samplers via `texture_external`, with frame-exact synchronization during offline headless video exports.

blocks.text: The `RTHTML` entity inherits from [`Model`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/Model.ts) and supports four distinct execution modes:

items: An invisible clipper container (`clipperElement`) is mounted over the canvas, restricting DOM visibility to canvas bounds.
The world-view-projection matrix of the active camera is decomposed into a CSS `matrix3d(...)` string:
The DOM element updates its 3D CSS transform each frame in exact synchronization with the camera, providing full browser-native text selection, mouse clicks, keyboard input, and interactive iframes.

blocks.text: Browsers forbid WebGPU from directly reading cross-origin DOM overlays. For headless frame-by-frame 4K video exports (`retiam render`):

items: The HTML DOM is serialized into an XML string.

blocks.code:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1024" height="768">
       <foreignObject width="100%" height="100%">
           <!-- Serialized DOM Markup -->
       </foreignObject>
   </svg>

items: Rasterized into an `ImageBitmap` and uploaded to the GPU texture array, ensuring embedded HTML participates in shadows, depth testing, and raytracing.

blocks.text: C. 3D Pointer Raycasting to DOM Forwarding
When the user clicks or moves the mouse over the 3D canvas:

items: The [`Raycaster`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/utils/Raycaster.ts) calculates the barycentric intersection coordinate $(u, v) \in [0, 1]^2$ on the quad surface.
The internal pixel target is resolved:

blocks.tex: x_{\text{dom}} = u \cdot W_{\text{element}}, \quad y_{\text{dom}} = (1 - v) \cdot H_{\text{element}}

items: A synthetic `PointerEvent` or `MouseEvent` is dispatched to `document.elementFromPoint(x, y)`, providing interactive typing and clicking directly on 3D floating monitors.

blocks.text: `RTVideo` maps HTML5 `<video>` frame decoders to WebGPU textures:

items: **Suppression of Flash-to-White**: Initializes with black emission (`emStrength: 0.0`) until `video.readyState >= 2` (HAVE_CURRENT_DATA) to prevent white frames during asynchronous loading.

**Deterministic Headless Sync**: During offline rendering ([`OfflineRenderManager.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/OfflineRenderManager.ts)), normal playback is paused. `RTVideo` explicitly steps the video element's time (`video.currentTime = scene.time`) and awaits the `seeked` event before encoding each video frame.
